rationale: The exposure must be read by hand from paper drug records, and the investigator has 60 hours of reading time, so sampling cases and controls is far more efficient than reading every record. Rescue treatment is well captured in the recovery log (c3), which gives a clean case definition, and a similar case-control analysis answered this question elsewhere (c2). Adherence is likely to be partial (c1), so exposure among controls will be common enough for a precise estimate. Controls come from the same operating lists to match on surgeon, anaesthetist and case mix.
alternatives: Reading every record from six months of lists (refused: about 3,000 records exceed the 60 hours available)
Prospective recording of prophylaxis on a new form (refused: new data collection is outside the stated constraints and would change behaviour)
whyNotMoreComplex: A trial of adherence support would need the local association first; the case-control study provides it with existing records.

decision.statement: Conduct a case-control study with controls from the same operating lists, reading anaesthetic records to classify prophylaxis against the protocol, to estimate the association of under-prophylaxis with rescue treatment for nausea or vomiting.
decision.question: Should the unit estimate the association between prophylaxis adherence and rescue treatment with a case-control study of existing records?

criteria.text: Adherence is likely partial, a similar design found an association elsewhere, and the nausea log gives a workable case definition.
The reading time needed exceeds the 60 hours available.

gates.requirement: Health records approval for access to scanned anaesthetic records
gates.evidence: Approval HR-2026-118 dated 2026-09-09, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Research ethics board decision on secondary use of records with a waiver of consent

decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c3; the ethics board application has not been submitted, so the action stays blocked.

summary: Case-control study recommended; the decision rests on three ledger claims and waits for the ethics decision.
